original_value: Magnetization reversal in a Wiegand wire induces a pulse voltage in the pickup coil around the wire, called the Wiegand pulse. The Wiegand sensor features the Wiegand wire and the pickup coil. The amplitude and width of the Wiegand pulse are independent of the frequency of the magnetic-field change. The pulse is generated by the Wiegand sensor, which facilitates the use of the Wiegand sensor as a power supply for equipment without batteries. In order to meet the power consumption requirements, it is necessary to maximize the energy of the pulse signal from the Wiegand sensor, without changing the external field conditions. The distributions of the magnetic field generated from the applied magnet in air and in the Wiegand wire were simulated before the experiments. Simulation predicted an increase in the magnetic flux density through the center of the Wiegand wire. This study determined that the magnetic flux density through the center of the Wiegand wire, the position of the pickup coil, and the angle between the Wiegand sensor and the magnetic induction line were the main factors that affected the energy of a Wiegand pulse. The relationship between these factors and the energy of the Wiegand pulse were obtained.

result.paraphrase: When magnetization reverses in a Wiegand wire, it produces a pulse voltage in the surrounding pickup coil, known as the Wiegand pulse. A Wiegand sensor consists of the Wiegand wire and the pickup coil. The pulse amplitude and width do not depend on the frequency of magnetic-field variation. Because the sensor generates this pulse, it can be used as a power source for battery-free equipment. To satisfy power-consumption demands, the pulse energy from the Wiegand sensor must be maximized without altering external field conditions. Before the experiments, simulations were performed of the magnetic-field distribution produced by the applied magnet in air and in the Wiegand wire. The simulations predicted increased magnetic flux density through the center of the Wiegand wire. The study found that the magnetic flux density through the wire center, the pickup-coil position, and the angle between the Wiegand sensor and the magnetic induction line were the main factors affecting Wiegand pulse energy, and it established the relationships between these factors and pulse energy.
